claims.text: Salt mining extracts sodium chloride, commonly known as salt, from deposits found beneath the Earth's surface.
claims.label: salt from underground deposits

claims.text: The mining method used depends largely on the geological context of the deposit.
claims.label: geology choosing the method

claims.text: In solution mining, water is pumped into the salt deposit to dissolve the salt into a brine, which is pumped back to the surface and evaporated to crystallize the salt.
claims.label: solution mining with brine

claims.text: In underground mining, tunnels are excavated into the salt deposit much as in coal mining and the salt is extracted in large blocks or slabs.
claims.label: underground tunnel mining

claims.text: Rock salt is typically mined by room-and-pillar mining, which leaves supporting pillars of salt behind to keep the mine roof from collapsing.
claims.label: room-and-pillar support

claims.text: Solar salt evaporation, common in arid regions, uses the sun's heat to evaporate seawater and leave salt crystals behind.
claims.label: solar evaporation of seawater

claims.text: Salt mining requires careful attention to environmental impact, including brine disposal and limiting land disturbance, because operations can significantly alter the landscape and hydrology.
claims.label: the environmental impact
